## Coast Live Oak Data Analysis 

### Data Loading and Cleaning 

```{r}
#loading packages to use in this project
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r}
#reading in the soil moisture data 
Moist_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "Soil Moisture")

#reading in the SPAD data 
SPAD_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "SPAD", 
             na = "NA")
```

Now to Clean! First, the soil moisture data

```{r}
Moist_Data_Raw #view the data so I remember what I need to do to clean it 

#First, I need to remove all of the excess NA values at the bottom 
Soil_Data <- Moist_Data_Raw |> 
  drop_na(Date) |> 
  #Now, I am only interested in the date, block, treatment, and VWC% readings (three per block)
  select(Date, Block, Treatment, VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc) |> 
  #the VWC values are currently chr, and I need them in double format
  mutate(VWC1_perc= as.double(VWC1_perc)) |> 
  mutate(VWC2_perc = as.double(VWC2_perc)) |> 
  mutate(VWC3_perc = as.double(VWC3_perc)) |> 
  #Making date character so it'll work when I create a before/after column 
  mutate(Date = as.character(Date)) |> 
  #Since I'm doing rain event, I want a before/after categorical variable
  mutate(Before_After = case_when(
    Date == "2026-10-08" ~ "Before",
    Date == "2026-10-21" ~ "After"
  ))


#now that Ive done all of that, I also realized that I need one VWC per treatment/block combo (so each row)

Soil_Data <- Soil_Data |> 
  rowwise() |> 
  mutate(Soil_VWC = mean(c(VWC1_perc , VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc), na.rm = TRUE))
```

Next, the SPAD data

```{r}
SPAD_Data_Raw #viewing it so I can see what needs to be done 

#only include the rows for date, block, treatment, leaf 1-6, dead/alive
SPAD_Data <- SPAD_Data_Raw |> 
  select(Date, Block, Treatment, Dead_Alive, Leaf1, Leaf2, Leaf3, Leaf4, Leaf5, Leaf6) |> 
  #Making date character so it'll work when I create a before/after column 
  mutate(Date = as.character(Date)) |> 
  #create column for Before/After rain event 
  mutate(Before_After = case_when(
    Date == "2026-10-08" ~ "Before",
    Date == "2026-10-15" ~ "After"
  ))  |> 
  #filter out dead seedlings 
  filter(Dead_Alive == "Alive") |> 
  #now to create one SPAD reading for each sapling 
  rowwise() |> 
  mutate(mean_SPAD = mean(c(Leaf1, Leaf2, Leaf3, Leaf4, Leaf5, Leaf6), na.rm = TRUE))
```

### ANOVA

Testing the following relationship: SPAD \~ rain event \* habitat type

I want to test it with the interaction, as I expect the habitat type to have impacted how the rain water is received by the plant (the canopy/dead tree might keep it from getting as much rain, or might shield the soil from direct sunlight that would be causing evaporation).

In this section:

- Assumptions/ Normality tests

- ANOVA

- Figure

Assumptions Check

```{r}
#visualizing the data 
SPAD_Data |> 
  ggplot()+
  aes(x=Treatment, y = mean_SPAD, fill = Before_After)+
  geom_boxplot()
```

```{r}

# Build the linear model
SPAD_ANOVA_Model  <- lm(mean_SPAD ~ Treatment * Before_After, data = SPAD_Data)
#plot the model
plot(SPAD_ANOVA_Model, which = 2)
# Create a QQ plot of residuals
ggpubr::ggqqplot(residuals(SPAD_ANOVA_Model))

#run LAvene's test for homogeneity of variance 
plot(SPAD_ANOVA_Model, which = 1)

SPAD_Data |>  rstatix::levene_test(mean_SPAD ~ Treatment*Before_After)
```

Results of assumption check:

- Residuals of model look good

- P-value from Lavene's test is 0.009, so it is significant. I will move forward with doing the ANOVA, but will make note of this in the final paper.

Let's do the ANOVA!

```{r}
anova(SPAD_ANOVA_Model)

#I also want to create an aov model that I will use later in my Tukey HSD 
SPAD_Model_aov <- aov(mean_SPAD ~ Treatment * Before_After, data = SPAD_Data)
summary(SPAD_Model_aov)
```

The results we get tells us that Treatment has a significant effect on mean_SPAD, and Treatment combined with Before_After has a REALLY significant effect.

Now, which treatment/date combinations are statistically different?

```{r}
#Tukey HSD fo determine which pairs are different from each other 
TukeyHSD(SPAD_Model_aov)
```

Of the same treatment before-after pairs, the following are the only ones that were significant:

AC Before-After (p=0.04), OS Before-After (p=0.03)

Of the ones that were the same date, here are the significant ones:

OS Before-NR Before (p=0.03), OS Before - DT Before (p=0.001), OS Before-AC Before (p=0.00002)

There were other pairs that were statistically different. However, if they did not have an overlap (so were either the same date or the same micro habitat), I do not feel that it is important in my analysis.

Now for the figure!

```{r}
SPAD_Data |> 
  ggplot()+
  aes(x=Treatment, y = mean_SPAD, fill = fct_rev(Before_After))+
  geom_boxplot()+
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("Before"="skyblue", "After"="midnightblue")) +
  labs( y = "Leaf SPAD",
        x = "Microhabitat",
        title = "SPAD by Treatment and Rain Event",
        fill = "Relation to Rain Event") #labs is giving us labels on our graph 
```
